lines.en: Lovely evening, isn’t it? Are you here for the cultural night?
lines.pt: Noite linda, não é? Você veio para a noite cultural?

lines.en: Yes! Did you hear about the music show? **Apparently,** it starts at eight and it’s free.
lines.pt: Sim! Você ficou sabendo do show de música? Pelo visto começa às oito e é gratuito.

lines.en: I read that Hana is singing a Korean folk song. **Shall we** watch it together?
lines.pt: Li que a Hana vai cantar uma canção folclórica coreana. Vamos assistir juntos?

lines.en: **Sounds like a plan!** **Speaking of** music, have you ever heard Korean singing live?
lines.pt: Combinado! Falando em música, você já ouviu canto coreano ao vivo?

lines.en: Never! But I was walking here when I heard her practicing. It sounded beautiful.
lines.pt: Nunca! Mas eu estava vindo para cá quando a ouvi ensaiando. Soou lindo.

lines.en: Wonderful. Could you tell me how to get to the stage?
lines.pt: Maravilhoso. Você poderia me dizer como chegar ao palco?

lines.en: Go straight past the fountain. You can’t miss it.
lines.pt: Siga reto passando pela fonte. Você não tem como errar.

lines.en: Thanks! **By the way,** in my country people usually bring flowers to artists. I’ll buy some first.
lines.pt: Obrigada! A propósito, no meu país as pessoas costumam levar flores para os artistas. Vou comprar algumas antes.

lines.en: Great idea. **Let’s meet** at the stage at quarter to eight.
lines.pt: Ótima ideia. Vamos nos encontrar no palco às oito menos quinze.

pages.title: Real-Life Mission Day 12

situation.text: You arrive at a cultural evening in a plaza. In one evening you chat with a stranger, invite and decline, share news, tell a short story, ask for directions and explain a tradition.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can chain seven real-life situations in one evening, switching naturally between inviting, sharing experiences, telling stories, giving directions, sharing news and talking about traditions.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — A cultural evening
pages.intro: At a cultural event people mix small talk, curiosity and kindness. Look and guess before you read.

cards.note: The evening, the music or the weather are easy first topics.
Ask questions about where people are from and what they enjoy.
Food, music and stories are natural ways to connect with new people.

qs.q: How do you start a conversation at an event?
qs.pt: Como puxar conversa em um evento?

levels.B1: Comment on something you both see, then ask a light question.
levels.B2: Begin with a shared observation, then widen with an open question to find common ground.

qs.q: Why combine small talk with real information?
qs.pt: Por que unir conversa leve e informação real?

levels.B1: Small talk builds trust, and information makes the conversation useful.
levels.B2: Light talk builds rapport, while concrete details let the exchange lead to plans.

qs.q: How can you leave a conversation politely?
qs.pt: Como sair de uma conversa educadamente?

levels.A2: It was nice talking to you. See you later!
levels.B1: Say it was nice, give a reason or plan, and say goodbye.
levels.B2: A warm closing remark plus a reason to move on lets both people part comfortably.

pages.compare: In Brazil, cultural events (festas, shows in the praça) are social and people chat easily. In English, “Lovely evening, isn’t it?”, “Are you from here?” and “It was nice talking to you” do the same job. What would you add?

stretch: B2: compare eventos culturais no Brasil e nos EUA.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: Natural speech comes in short groups of words with a small pause between them: “By the way, | in my country, | people usually bring flowers.”

items.say: By the way, I’ll buy some flowers.
items.linked: By the WAY, | I’ll BUY some FLOW·ers.

items.say: Speaking of music, have you ever heard it?
items.linked: SPEAK·ing of MU·sic, | have-ya EV·er HEARD it?

opts: By the way, I’ll buy some flowers.
By the way I’ll buy some flowers soon.
Bye, the way I buy flowers.
identify.say: By the way, I’ll buy some flowers.

own.prompt: Write one sentence with a connector (By the way / Speaking of) about the evening.
own.criteria: Say it twice: word by word, then in thought groups. Which sounds more natural?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: grupos de pensamento (pausas curtas entre blocos).
solo: Escutar e identificar → repetir em blocos → frase própria.

group: Coro, depois duplas.
Cada estudante diz uma frase em blocos.
answers: Identify 1: By the way, I’ll buy some flowers. · Identify 2: Sounds like a plan!

errors.w: Falar palavra por palavra, sem blocos
errors.r: By the WAY, | I’ll BUY some FLOWers.

errors.w: Pausa no meio de “Sounds like a plan”

support: Reduza a velocidade e marque os blocos.

items.q: 1. You see a stranger at the plaza and want to start a chat.
2. A friend invites you, but you have a meeting. Choose the kind reply.
opts: I’d love to, but I have a meeting. Maybe next time!
No. I do not like it.

items.q: 3. You want to ask where the stage is.

items.q: 4. You want to tell about a tradition in your country.
opts: In my country, people usually bring flowers to artists.
People bring usually flowers in my country.

pages.title: Group mission — a cultural evening
pages.goal: Each group must live the whole evening in English: meet, invite, share, tell, give directions and talk about traditions.

missions.mission: Meet at the plaza: chat with a stranger, invite them to the music show, they decline, then agree on another plan. Ask where the stage is.
missions.constraint: Use at least four expressions from classes 87, 90 and 93.

missions.mission: Share news about the event, tell a short story about how you heard it and ask about a classmate’s travel experiences.
missions.constraint: Use “Apparently…”, “I was… when…” and “Have you ever…?”.

missions.mission: Present a tradition from your country, invite visitors to try a dish and give directions to the food stalls.
missions.constraint: Use “In my country…”, “It’s supposed to…” and “You can’t miss it.”

success: Use an expression from each assigned class.

teach.goal: Realizar a missão integrada: viver a noite inteira em inglês.
group: Cada grupo recebe papéis e restrições; alterne os papéis.
Progressão: com chunks, palavras-chave, sem roteiro.
Anote 2–3 correções por grupo e faça a devolutiva da unidade.
answers: Modelo: “Lovely evening, isn’t it?” → “Would you like to watch the music show?” → “I’d love to, but I have to meet a friend. Maybe next time.” → “Could you tell me how to get to the stage?”
extra: Which situation was the hardest to connect?
support: Dê o início de frase em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short message to a friend about the cultural evening: invite them, share one piece of news and give directions.
pages.model: Hi Hana! Would you like to come to the cultural evening in the plaza? Apparently, the music show starts at eight and it’s free. From the bank, go straight past the fountain; you can’t miss the stage. Let’s meet there at quarter to eight!
checklist: I shared news with Apparently or I read that.
I gave directions with a landmark.
I closed with a plan (Let’s meet…).
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points and show a more natural way to say the same idea.

teach.goal: Produção escrita integrada: convite, notícia e direções.
solo: Corrija 2–3 pontos prioritários.
group: Troquem as mensagens e respondam.
extra: Add a short story about how you heard of the event.
support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: The situation stays the same; the language grows in length, nuance and autonomy.

ladder.say: Shall we watch the show? Sounds like a plan!
ladder.goal: Suggest and agree on a plan.

ladder.say: By the way, did you hear about the show? Apparently it’s free, so shall we go together?
Speaking of music, I’ve been wanting to see her perform; I read that tickets are free, so it would be a shame to miss it.
I’ve never been one for crowds, but given the reviews, I’m inclined to make an exception tonight.
Rarely does a free evening promise so much; I’d say we owe it to ourselves to go.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.
